text:
carmen: FYI spun up cobalt-bridge-13b int8 candidate on staging. Token savings look excellent but we're seeing a subtle "coverage" regression on multi-step synthesis flows. Need a concise scorecard for GTN+PM.

ben: paste smoke numbers pls.

carmen: smoke dump:
```
fp16 baseline: cost_per_token = $0.0109, p95 = 158ms, baseline_accept = 0.82
int8 candidate: cost_per_token = $0.0033, p95 = 174ms, accept = 0.71
long_recall (5k) = -9.5pp, short_recall (256) = -1.2pp
kv-cache hit rate = 81% on sampled trace
```

yuki: 3.3x token cost reduction, nice. But -9.5pp long recall is large. Failure mode? omissions, truncated enumerations, or hallucination?

carmen: mostly omissions / missing bullets in enumerations. Not much hallucination (<0.5pp). Prompt-amplification recovers ~2pp.

ben: ran hybrid where attention + layernorm kept fp16 and matmuls int8. microbench: recall recovered ~5.1pp, cost +18% vs int8 (still ~2.7x cheaper than fp16). p95 +8ms.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary started cobalt-bridge-13b-int8 in us-west-2 (1 GPU). dashboard: https://internal/dash/models/cobalt-bridge-13b/int8

carmen: kicked off 400-sample labeled eval on synthesis and meeting slices; will post results when done.

ben: for GTN include unit econ table for avg_tokens = [250, 800, 1600] and per-request savings. simple calc example: avg_t=800 -> savings_per_req = (0.0109 - 0.0033)*800 = $5.68.

yuki: add LTV sensitivity rows: if conversion sensitivity is 1pp, 5pp, 10pp for critical flows. GTN will need those.

carmen: drafting scorecard fields: [variant, cost_per_token, p95_latency, recall_long_pp, recall_short_pp, accept_delta_pp, recommended_route, rollout_gates, notes]. Will include quick sims.

ben: rollout idea: default hybrid for 600+ token outputs, int8 for ephemeral/drafts, fp16 for final exports and flagged premium customers. Route-by-intent + estimated_output_tokens heuristic.

yuki: propose gating rules: recall_long >= -7pp AND hallucination_increase <= 1pp on 24h rolling; auto-rollback if accept_delta > 4pp over 12h. Also require 2k-sample A/B on labeled slices before >25% traffic shift.

ops-bot: eval job complete (400 samples) -> https://internal/evals/cobalt-bridge-13b/int8/400

carmen: quick eval TL;DR: int8 long_recall = -8.9pp, hallucination +0.4pp, accept_drop = 4.0pp. hybrid long_recall = -3.8pp, hallucination +0.3pp, accept_drop = 1.6pp. numbers noisy.

ben: economic calc table (rounded):
```
avg_tokens | fp16_cost | int8_cost | hybrid_cost | savings_fp16->int8 | savings_fp16->hybrid
250        | $2.73     | $0.83     | $1.00      | $1.90              | $1.73
800        | $8.72     | $2.64     | $3.20      | $6.08              | $5.52
1600       | $17.44    | $5.28     | $6.40      | $12.16             | $11.04
```

yuki: include greyscale scenario: if recall loss causes 3% drop in conversion on those flows with avg LTV $20, lost_rev_per_req = 0.03*20 = $0.60. Compare to savings_per_req.

carmen: good call. I'll add a break-even table that computes required conversion drop to negate savings.

ben: add monitoring hooks: rolling labeled-slice evals, priming-sensitivity metric (how often a 1-line priming fix moves a prediction from bad->ok), and active canary rollback if accept_drop >3pp for flagged slices over 6h.

ops-bot: alert: INF-4199 created to track canary, eval CSV, scorecard, and A/B plan.

yuki: GTN note suggestion: keep variant names explicit (fp16 / int8 / hybrid-attn-fp16). Provide a short decision matrix: if expected_output_tokens > 1200 -> prefer fp16 or hybrid pinned; if intent=="export" -> fp16; else hybrid default; fallback to fp16 on repeat edits.

carmen: will upload sample failures and scorecard to INF-4199. Also including a small prompt tweak doc where a single added instruction recovered 2-4pp on some items.

ben: one practical tip: for customers with tight budgets, consider a staged rollout: hybrid -> 30% traffic for 7d -> monitor -> increase. avoids big conv shocks.

yuki: I'll draft the GTN brief and include the break-even sims plus the A/B plan and routing flags. Aim to present to PMs tomorrow.

carmen: final note: 400-sample is noisy; recommend 2k-sample A/B on production-labeled slices before any >30% reallocation. Posting scorecard in INF-4199 now. :spiral_notepad:
